Enter a value, press Enter to keep the current choice, or type q to cancel. Boolean settings use yes / no; y / n and true / false also work. update-check defaults to yes when no value is saved; a saved no stays selected. Its explanation states that release checks contact GitHub. Invalid answers show an error and ask again, keeping your earlier answers. A final [y/N] confirms the review. Nothing is saved before that confirmation; q or EOF cancels without saving. Saved overrides stay selected unless you change them. Reviewed settings that have been removed are deleted from preferences only after confirmation; unknown keys not found in the previous review still require manual repair.

The receipt lives in ~/.astrona/settings-review.json, separate from preferences and usage-term acceptance. It records the reviewed definitions and CLI version, not a server identity or tracking token. Writes share the settings lock and use private atomic files. If interrupted between saving choices and the receipt, the next explicit review asks again. data reset --yes clears both files. Unsetting update-check restores its default yes without requiring another review.

Review does not enable telemetry or account tracking; existing signed-in lab progress tracking is separate. Usage terms and remote-code trust retain their own approval requirements.

CI and scripts do not need a settings review step or a pinned review ID. If you choose to run settings review without a terminal, it still requires explicit approval. Set any overrides, inspect the view, then acknowledge its exact ID:

astrona settings set update-check no
astrona settings view
astrona settings review --accept <review-id-you-inspected>

The ID binds to definitions and saved choices, so it changes when either changes. Do not pipe a newly generated ID straight into --accept; keep the reviewed ID in CI configuration and update it after inspecting changes. For a fresh runner, use the ID displayed with that runner's exact saved settings, before review pins additional defaults. Optional settings review does not remove the separate per-command CI requirement for --accept-terms.

Cache limits are local preferences, not lab flags, and are not forwarded during version handover. Older CLI releases that validate settings may reject these new keys; remove the overrides or upgrade that binary before using it.

docs.title: Start Labs from the Website
docs.text: astrona connect keeps this computer connected to the Astrona site. While it runs, Start on my machine on a lab page builds that lab here, and the page follows its progress. You don't need to type the lab name or keep a terminal next to the browser.

docs.title: Connect a computer
docs.text:
Sign in first, then connect:

astrona login
astrona connect

astrona connect prints a line when it connects and one for every request from the website, followed by that command's own output. It keeps running until you press Ctrl+C. If the network drops, it reconnects by itself: it retries after about a second, waits up to a minute between tries, and spreads the retries out at random. Each new connection tells the site how the previous one ended, so support can see drops.

Pressing Ctrl+C while the website's command runs stops it the way Ctrl+C stops astrona run at a terminal: a lab that is being built stops at the next step, removes what this run created, and the lab page shows that the build failed. astrona connect waits for that, up to two minutes, before it exits. Press Ctrl+C a second time to quit at once; anything left over is then removed by astrona destroy.

docs.title: Confirm each request
docs.text:
astrona connect --confirm

asks in the terminal before each request from the website runs, for example:

The website asks to build and start ATS000/section-010/module-01/lab-01 on this computer. Allow? [y/N]

Type y to run it. Anything else, or no answer within two minutes, refuses it, and the lab page shows that the request was declined on this computer. Status requests run without asking because they change nothing. --confirm needs a terminal, so it can't be combined with --install.

docs.title: Start with your login session
docs.text:
To have it start with your login session:

astrona connect --install     # macOS LaunchAgent, or Linux systemd user service
astrona connect --uninstall

The installed service writes to ~/.astrona/logs/connect.log. It uses the PATH of the shell you installed it from, so it finds Docker or Podman and kind the same way. On Linux the user service runs while you are logged in; loginctl enable-linger keeps it running after you log out. --install isn't available on Windows yet.

Stopping the service (logging out, --uninstall) also lets a running lab build clean up first. If another astrona connect takes the connection over, the service exits with an error, and the service manager starts it again about ten seconds later, so it takes the connection back. To run astrona connect in a terminal for longer, run astrona connect --uninstall first. If this computer is signed out, the service stops and stays stopped; sign in with astrona login, then run astrona connect --install again.

docs.title: What the website can ask for
docs.text:
Only these commands, each for one catalog lab named like ATS000/section-010/module-01/lab-01:

Request Runs Start astrona run <lab> --yes --no-browser, taking over the lab session the website created Status astrona status <lab> Submit astrona submit <lab>: it ends the attempt, pass or fail, and deletes the lab Reset astrona reset <lab> --yes Destroy astrona destroy <lab> Stop / Start astrona stop <lab> / astrona start <lab> Renew astrona run renew <lab>

Renew gives a running playground its full time limit again, as astrona run renew does at a terminal. For a lab that isn't a running playground it fails with renew's own error, and the page shows it.

astrona connect checks the command and the lab name before anything runs and refuses everything else: shell commands, local paths, URLs and other options never travel over the connection. Each command runs without a terminal, in an empty working directory, one at a time. Anything that would need an answer from you fails rather than waiting. Accept the CLI terms once at a terminal first.

docs.title: What the page shows while it builds
docs.text: The lab page lists each stage of the build as it starts: the lab's cluster, images, add-ons, setup scripts, manifests and readiness checks. For a lab with linked clusters it also shows each cluster as it is created and when it is ready, so a long multi-cluster build doesn't look stuck. Running astrona settings set parallel 3 on that computer creates up to three linked clusters at a time, for the website as for astrona run.

docs.title: Your computers
docs.text:
astrona devices

lists every computer signed in to your account. This one is marked *, and online means it is running astrona connect. To rename a computer, choose the one lab pages preselect, or sign one out, go to Settings → Devices on the website. Signing out a computer that is connected ends its connection and removes its sign-in. astrona connect then stops and doesn't reconnect.

Only one astrona connect runs per computer. Starting a second one takes the connection over, and the first one stops, unless it is the installed service, which starts again and takes the connection back.

docs.title: Lab Config Schema
docs.text: The full shape of config.yaml (internal/config.LabConfig). Every field is optional unless noted — an empty/omitted block simply means that stage does nothing.

docs.title: Editor support and validation
docs.text:
Add this first line to a lab's config.yaml for autocompletion, hover docs and inline errors in VS Code (with the Red Hat YAML extension) and any other editor using yaml-language-server:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://cli.astrona.io/schema/lab-config.schema.json

The JSON Schema is generated from astrona's own config types, so it always matches what the CLI accepts — every object rejects unknown keys, and closed value sets (runtime.type, type: file|folder|url, check types, …) are enums. It expects the documented spelling (podReady); the CLI itself also accepts other letter case for check and source types.

From the command line:

astrona validate -c ./labs/my-lab

checks the config without creating anything and exits non-zero on any problem — good as a CI step for lab repositories:

  ✗  line 3                                 unknown field "waitfor" in bootstrap/testing
        fix: did you mean "waitFor"?
  ✗  validation.checks[1]                   unsupported type 'httpGet' (resourceExists, podReady or command)
  ✗  teardown.init[0] cleanup               local file source does not exist: …/cleanup.sh

Unknown fields (typos like waitfor or manifest) used to be silently ignored, leaving a lab without the gates or manifests its author meant to configure. Now astrona validate and astrona check fail on them, and run/test/submit print a warning with a did-you-mean (they still run, so a lab that has always worked keeps working).

docs.title: Top level
docs.text:
apiVersion: astrona.io/v1   # config format (optional; a newer one is refused)
astronaVersion: ">=0.2.0"   # which astrona releases may run this lab (optional) — see Astrona Versions
metadata: {}     # MetadataConfig
runtime: {}      # RuntimeConfig — omit entirely for a kind cluster
bootstrap: {}    # BootstrapConfig
testing: {}      # BootstrapConfig (same shape, CI-only)
validation: {}   # ValidationConfig
teardown: {}     # TeardownConfig
resources: []    # LabResource — optional; everything in resources/ counts without it
tabs: []         # Tab — optional; the browser workspace's tabs (kind only)

docs.title: metadata
docs.text:
Field Type Description name string Lab name — becomes the cluster/VM name, prefixed astro-. Must start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, digits, ., _ and - (no /, ,, spaces or ..) — see Names docs.question string The task statement. Default: question.md next to config.yaml, if it exists docs.solution string The full step-by-step walkthrough. Default: solution.md docs.prerequisites string What to know before starting. Default: prerequisites.md docs.caseStudy string A softer, hint-driven version of the same task. Default: case-study.md timeLimit duration Playgrounds only: how long a module's playground may run before its clock stops and its cluster is removed, written like 90m, 2h or 1h30m; between 5m and 24h. Empty: the site's default (2h). Ignored for labs, which have no such limit — see Playgrounds

docs is optional: a doc it doesn't list is found by its default file name next to config.yaml, so a lab with question.md and solution.md beside its config needs no docs block at all. The older names examQuestion (= question) and guide (= solution) still work; setting both names of the same doc to different files is an error. Doc paths are relative to config.yaml and must stay inside the lab directory (absolute paths are rejected); students read them with astrona docs.

docs.title: Names
docs.text: metadata.name, runtime.qemu[].name and runtime.kind.clusters[].name become directory names under ~/.astrona/ (state that astrona destroy deletes) and parts of qemu command lines, so they must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ and must not contain ... Every command checks this when it loads the config and refuses the lab otherwise, e.g. metadata.name: invalid name 'x/../y': must start with a letter or digit …. (runtime.kind.clusters[].name has a stricter rule of its own, below.) astrona bundle load applies the same rule to the lab name recorded in a bundle.

docs.title: runtime
docs.text: Field Type Description type string ""/"kind" (default) or "qemu" kind Kind cluster kind only — node image, node count, networking. Omit for kind's defaults qemu list of QEMU VM Required when type: qemu; always a list, even for one VM networks list {name, cidr} — named virtual network segments VMs can join portForwards list of PortForward kind only — host-side port forwards started by astrona run

docs.title: runtime.portForwards[N]
docs.text:
kind only (rejected for type: qemu). Each entry becomes a background, auto-restarting kubectl port-forward on 127.0.0.1, started once bootstrap (scripts, manifests and waitFor gates) has finished. See Port forwards.

Field Type Description name string Required. Unique, lowercase DNS label (a-z, 0-9, -) — shown in astrona port-forward list resource string Required. <kind>/<name>, kind one of svc/service, pod/po, deploy/deployment, sts/statefulset, rs/replicaset — e.g. svc/frontend namespace string Namespace of resource (default default) hostPort int Required. Local port, 1024–65535, unique within the lab. Always bound to 127.0.0.1 targetPort int Required. Port on the service/pod, 1–65535 scheme string http | https | tcp (default) — only changes the URL printed after run description string Optional, printed next to the URL after run cluster string Forward from a linked cluster (its name) instead of the lab's own — e.g. an identity provider's login page 
runtime:
  type: kind
  portForwards:
    - name: web
      resource: svc/frontend
      hostPort: 8080
      targetPort: 80
      scheme: http
      description: Frontend UI
    - name: db
      resource: svc/postgres
      namespace: data
      hostPort: 5432
      targetPort: 5432

docs.title: runtime.qemu[N]
docs.text:
Field Type Description name string Required once there's more than one entry; leave empty for a single-VM lab. Same character rule as metadata.name — see Names image.type string "file" | "url" | "oci" image.source string Path, URL, or OCI reference, depending on type. A file path must be relative to the lab directory and stay inside it (no absolute paths, no .. or symlinks leading out) image.checksum string e.g. sha256:... — recommended image.checksums map Alternative: per-algorithm checksum map arch string Guest architecture cpus int vCPU count memoryMB int Memory in MB diskSizeGB int Overlay disk size in GB extraDisks list {sizeGB, format, serial} — additional blank disks networks list {name, ipv4} — attaches a NIC to a runtime.networks segment sshAccess list of strings Other VM names this VM can SSH into passwordlessly (multi-VM only) sshPort int Host-side forwarded SSH port sshPasswordAuth bool Enable password auth in addition to key auth, for the student account only — the astrona automation account (see Runtimes) is always key-auth only display bool Show a QEMU display window bootstrap BootstrapConfig init scripts that run only against this VM, right after the shared root bootstrap.init on it (in a single-VM lab too) validation ValidationConfig Graded only against this VM, after the shared root validation: its command checks and scripts run inside this VM, http checks from this machine. Results are suffixed (name) in a multi-VM lab. passPercent is not allowed here (astrona validate fails): the root validation.passPercent is the lab's one pass mark

See Runtimes for single- vs multi-VM behavior.

docs.title: Disk device naming
docs.text:
Disks are attached in a fixed order, so the guest device names are stable:

Guest device Disk /dev/vda Main overlay disk (root filesystem, diskSizeGB). Always the boot disk. /dev/vdb extraDisks[0] /dev/vdc extraDisks[1] ... ...

The cloud-init seed disk is also attached but carries no useful mount for a lab. /dev/vda is guaranteed to be the boot disk regardless of how many extraDisks entries are present.

For labs that must not hard-code a /dev/vd* name, set a serial on the extraDisks entry and reference it by the stable /dev/disk/by-id/virtio-<serial> path instead.

docs.title: runtime.kind
docs.text:
kind only (rejected for type: qemu). Omit it and the lab gets a plain kind create cluster: one control-plane node, kind's default node image, kindnet CNI. Every field is optional.

Field Type Description version string Kubernetes version, e.g. v1.31.2 — boots kindest/node:<version>. Mutually exclusive with image image string Full node image reference. Pin by digest for reproducible labs: kindest/node:v1.31.2@sha256:… dnsTimeout string CoreDNS readiness timeout before bootstrap; default 3m, allowed 1s–30m. Also supported on linked clusters. A longer timeout helps slow startup but cannot repair an unhealthy control plane nodes.controlPlanes int 1–3 (default 1). More than one adds kind's load balancer container nodes.workers int 0–6 (default 0) networking.disableDefaultCNI bool Don't install kindnet — the lab installs its own CNI (Calico, Cilium, …) in bootstrap. Nodes stay NotReady until it does networking.kubeProxyMode string iptables | ipvs | nftables | none networking.ipFamily string ipv4 | ipv6 | dual networking.podSubnet string Pod CIDR, e.g. 192.168.0.0/16 (Calico's default) networking.serviceSubnet string Service CIDR; must not overlap podSubnet featureGates map[string]bool Kubernetes feature gates, e.g. InPlacePodVerticalScaling: true runtimeConfig map[string]string API groups to enable/disable ("true"/"false"), e.g. "resource.k8s.io/v1beta1": "true" addons Addons Cluster components installed right after the cluster is created preloadImages list of strings Images loaded into every node before addons/bootstrap, e.g. [nginx:1.27-alpine] — explicit tag or digest required (not :latest), max 30. See Preloaded images clusters list of KindCluster Extra kind clusters running side by side with the lab's own (max 5). Called labs before v0.3 — still accepted, with a deprecation warning sharedCA bool Give the lab its own certificate authority, installed in its cluster and every linked cluster: ConfigMap astrona-ca (ca.crt) in default; with the certManager addon a ClusterIssuer astrona-ca. Scripts, command checks and astrona shell get $ASTRONA_CA_CERT. See TLS between clusters 
runtime:
  type: kind
  kind:
    version: v1.31.2
    nodes:
      workers: 2
    networking:
      disableDefaultCNI: true
      podSubnet: 192.168.0.0/16

docs.title: runtime.kind.addons
docs.text:
Installed in this order, right after the cluster is created and before bootstrap; each one is waited on until ready. Each is pinned to one upstream release whose manifest checksum is built into astrona — see Addons.

Field Type Description cni string calico (Calico v3.32.2). Implies networking.disableDefaultCNI: true and pod subnet 192.168.0.0/16 (set podSubnet to that or leave it out). Enforces NetworkPolicy certManager bool cert-manager v1.21.2 metricsServer bool metrics-server v0.9.0 (kubectl top, HPA), with --kubelet-insecure-tls for kind's self-signed kubelet certs gatewayAPI string envoy — Gateway API CRDs + Envoy Gateway v1.9.2, with GatewayClass eg gatewayPorts.http int Host port for Gateway listeners on port 80 (default 8080, on 127.0.0.1) gatewayPorts.https int Host port for Gateway listeners on port 443 (default 8443, on 127.0.0.1) 
runtime:
  kind:
    nodes: { workers: 1 }
    addons:
      cni: calico
      certManager: true
      metricsServer: true
      gatewayAPI: envoy        # Gateways with gatewayClassName: eg

docs.title: runtime.kind.clusters[N]
docs.text:
Extra kind clusters that run side by side with the lab's own — e.g. an identity provider, a database, a second "site". They belong to the lab: astrona run creates them first, and stop, start, reset, destroy and test handle them together with the lab. See the Linked Labs guide.

Field Type Description name string Required. How the lab refers to the cluster: ASTRONA_CLUSTER_<NAME>_* env vars, astrona-clusters ConfigMap keys, cluster: on checks. Lowercase letters, digits, -; max 20 characters; unique. The kind cluster is astro-<lab>-<name> version, image, nodes, networking, featureGates, runtimeConfig, addons, preloadImages Same as for the lab's own cluster (above). A gateway addon gets no host ports here bootstrap BootstrapConfig Sets this cluster up — runs before the lab's own bootstrap testing BootstrapConfig This cluster's part of the reference solution — astrona test applies it before the lab's own testing teardown.init list of ResourceItem Best-effort scripts run before the lab is destroyed: after the lab's own teardown, in reverse start order, with KUBECONFIG pointing at this cluster. (Whether clusters are kept is the lab's teardown.keepCluster) wan.latency / wan.jitter string Simulate a remote site: latency added per round trip (e.g. 80ms) and its variation (10ms, needs latency) — see Simulating a remote site wan.loss string Share of packets dropped, 0%–100% wan.rate string Bandwidth cap, e.g. 10mbit (kbit, mbit, gbit) dependsOn list of strings Other linked clusters (names) that must be up and ready — bootstrap and waitFor done — before this one is created. Its scripts get their ASTRONA_CLUSTER_* addresses (and its cluster their astrona-clusters ConfigMap). Unknown names, self-dependencies and cycles are rejected

Paths are relative to the lab's config, like everywhere else; by convention each cluster keeps its files in clusters/<name>/ (clusters/idp/bootstrap/, clusters/idp/testing/).

Clusters are created one at a time: dependencies first, otherwise in the order listed; the lab's own cluster last. The first one that fails stops the run — nothing depending on it is started.

runtime:
  type: kind
  kind:
    clusters:
      - name: idp
        preloadImages: [nginx:1.27-alpine]
        bootstrap:
          manifests:
            - {name: idp, type: file, source: clusters/idp/bootstrap/idp.yaml}
          waitFor:
            - {resource: deploy/idp, namespace: auth}

The node image must exist for the kind version installed on the student's machine — each kind release lists the node images built for it. Kind config features that reach outside the cluster (extraMounts, extraPortMappings, kubeadmConfigPatches) are deliberately not exposed — see Runtimes.

docs.title: bootstrap / testing
docs.text:
Both use the same shape (BootstrapConfig) — testing only runs under astrona test.

Field Type Description init list of ResourceItem Scripts run in order at start manifests list of ResourceItem Applied via kubectl apply (requires a kubectl-reachable cluster) waitFor list of WaitFor Readiness gates checked in order after manifests (kind only)

docs.title: WaitFor
docs.text:
One readiness gate. Target exactly one of: a named object (resource: deploy/web), every object matching a label selector (resource: pod + selector), or every object of a kind (resource: nodes + all: true).

Field Type Description name string Optional label shown while waiting (defaults to the target) resource string Required. <kind>/<name>, or a bare <kind> with selector/all. CRD kinds work too: certificates.cert-manager.io/web-tls selector string Label selector, e.g. app=web or tier in (fe,be) all bool Every object of resource's kind namespace string Default default (ignored for cluster-scoped kinds like nodes) condition string rollout (kubectl rollout status) or a status condition for kubectl wait --for=condition=<X> (Ready, Available, Complete, Established, …) timeout string Go duration, 1s–30m (default 2m)

Default condition by kind — any other kind must set one:

Kind Default condition deploy/deployment, sts/statefulset, ds/daemonset rollout pod, node Ready job Complete crd/customresourcedefinition Established 
bootstrap:
  waitFor:
    - resource: nodes
      all: true                 # e.g. after bootstrap installed a CNI
      timeout: 3m
    - resource: deploy/web
      namespace: shop
    - name: database
      resource: pod
      selector: app=postgres
      namespace: shop
      timeout: 5m

While a gate's target doesn't exist yet (NotFound, no matching resources, kind not registered yet) it's retried every 2s until the timeout; any other kubectl failure fails the gate immediately. rollout only works for deployments, statefulsets and daemonsets, and needs a name or selector.

docs.title: validation
docs.text:
Field Type Description checks list of ValidationCheck Declarative checks script ResourceItem Single custom pass/fail script scripts list of ResourceItem Additional scripts, run after script, in order passPercent int 1–100: pass once the score reaches this percentage (e.g. 66). Unset: every check and script must pass. Root validation only — rejected in a runtime.qemu[].validation block

Validation scripts also take hint and points (see ValidationCheck). A lab needs at least one check or script to be graded — without any, submit/test exit 1 (astrona validate warns). On a qemu lab, a script's exit code 255 means SSH couldn't reach the VM and is a grading error, not a fail.

docs.title: ValidationCheck
docs.text: Field Type Description name string Label shown in the Proctor's report type string "resourceExists" | "podReady" | "command" | "jsonpath" | "count" | "http" — see Grading resource string kubectl get arguments (for resourceExists/podReady/jsonpath/count, required), e.g. deploy/web -n shop or pods -l app=web -n shop. The only flags allowed are -n/--namespace, -l/--selector, --field-selector and -A/--all-namespaces; no value may start with -. These four check types need a kind lab — a qemu lab has no cluster for them command string Shell words to run directly, no shell interpolation (for command) expect string Exact expected value (trimmed stdout / JSONPath value / body) contains string Value must contain this expectRegex string Value must match this regular expression (Go syntax) jsonpath string jsonpath checks: kubectl JSONPath, e.g. {.spec.replicas} min / max int count checks: bounds on the number of objects (at least one required) url string http checks: http:// or https:// URL expectStatus int http checks: expected status (default 200) hint string Shown to the student only when this check fails — a nudge, not the answer points int Weight in the score (default 1) cluster string Grade the check in this linked cluster (a runtime.kind.clusters name) instead of the lab's own. Not for http checks timeout duration How long the check may run, e.g. 30s or 2m; between 1s and 30m. Default 1m (http: 10s; podReady: waits 60s). Past it the check is stopped, with everything it started, and fails with timed out after …. For podReady it is also how long kubectl wait waits for readiness

docs.title: exam
docs.text:
Turns the lab into a timed exam. Omit it for normal practice labs.

Field Type Description timeLimit string Go duration, 1m–24h, e.g. 2h. The clock starts when astrona run (or reset) has the lab ready hideHints bool astrona submit never shows check hints strict bool A submission after the time limit can't pass

See Grading → Exam mode.

docs.title: teardown
docs.text: Field Type Description init list of ResourceItem Best-effort scripts run before the environment is destroyed keepCluster bool For a lab from your own files: astrona destroy skips destroying the environment (linked clusters included) after teardown scripts run. Ignored for a catalog lab or a run with a lab session, and by astrona submit and astrona reset, which always remove it

docs.title: resources
docs.text:
Files and folders a student shows, copies or runs with astrona resource instead of copying commands or file contents out of the lab's docs. They live in a resources/ folder next to config.yaml; every file or folder directly in it is a resource even without an entry here. An entry adds a description and says how it runs:

resources:
  - file: setup-db.sh              # resources/setup-db.sh — runs with bash (from .sh)
    description: Creates the demo database the task starts from
  - file: broken-deployment.yaml
    description: The Deployment you'll fix in step 2
    type: file                     # only shown or copied, never applied
  - file: load-test                # a folder
    description: Generates traffic so you can watch the HPA
    run: go run .                  # run in the folder
Field Type Description file string Required. Path inside resources/ (a file or folder; may be nested, e.g. tools/check.sh). Absolute paths and .. are refused description string One line shown when the lab starts and in astrona resource run string Command astrona resource run starts, in the resource's folder. Without it: .sh → bash, .yaml/.yml → kubectl apply -f against the lab (kind labs), an executable with #! → itself, anything else (and folders) → a file type file Never run — only shown or copied (run must be empty) vm string qemu labs: the VM it runs in (a runtime.qemu[].name)

A resource's short name is its file name without the extension (setup-db.sh → setup-db); the full relative filename also works in resource commands. Short names must be unique and use letters, digits, ., _, -. Hidden files (.DS_Store, .gitkeep) are skipped; symlinks are refused anywhere — the file itself, a linked folder in the middle of its path (home/.ssh/id_ed25519 with home a link) or anything inside a folder resource — and every read stays inside resources/. Also refused: more than 1000 files, a file over 50 MB or more than 200 MB in all.

astrona run / reset copy the resources to ~/.astrona/resources/<lab>/ (owner-only) before the lab is built — nothing in them runs — and list them once the lab is ready. A new run replaces the copy; astrona destroy removes it (--keep-resources keeps it). A config fetched from a URL has no folder, so it can't have resources — use a local lab or --git. astrona validate checks them. Students use them with astrona resource.

docs.title: tabs
docs.text:
kind only. The tabs of the browser workspace's right panel. The first tab is always the focus tab: a terminal on the lab's own cluster, named main. The entries here come after it, in order. The learner switches between tabs but cannot add or close one, and nothing outside this list is ever opened.

Tabs are configured per lab. Without tabs, the workspace shows only the focus tab. With tabs, it shows exactly the focus tab and these: a linked cluster gets a terminal tab only when you list it here.

runtime:
  type: kind
  kind:
    clusters:
      - name: edge
        config: ../edge
  portForwards:
    - name: web
      resource: svc/frontend
      hostPort: 8080
      targetPort: 80
      scheme: http
tabs:
  - name: edge                # a second terminal, on the linked cluster "edge"
    title: Edge cluster
    type: terminal
    cluster: edge
  - name: shop                # the lab's own app, through the port forward "web"
    title: Shop
    type: browser
    portForward: web
    path: /cart
  - name: netpol-docs         # documentation, shown inside the tab
    title: NetworkPolicy docs
    type: docs
    url: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/
  - name: cheatsheet          # Markdown shipped with the lab
    title: Cheat sheet
    type: docs
    file: docs/cheatsheet.md
Field Type Description name string Required. Unique, lowercase DNS label. main is reserved for the focus tab title string Required. What the tab shows; one line, at most 40 characters type terminal | browser | docs Required. cluster string terminal: a runtime.kind.clusters name; empty for the lab's own cluster (another shell next to the focus tab) portForward string browser: a runtime.portForwards name with scheme: http or https path string browser: the path to open, starting with / (default /) url string docs: an https:// documentation page. Either url or file file string docs: a Markdown file relative to config.yaml, at most 64 KiB, rendered like the task. Never the solution

What each type does:

  • terminal: an isolated shell like the focus tab's, on the lab's own cluster or a linked one. Each tab has one shell; when it ends, the tab offers to open a new one. Switching tabs keeps it running.
  • browser: the page a port forward serves, shown in a sandboxed frame with Back to start and Open in new window. Only the lab's own forwards on 127.0.0.1 can be shown; the workspace never proxies other hosts.
  • docs with url: the page, shown inside the tab in a sandboxed frame. Back to start returns to url wherever the learner navigated; Open in new window shows it in a separate window. Some documentation sites refuse to be shown inside another page (X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors): their tab stays blank, and the page cannot detect that, so a docs tab always notes it next to Open in new window. Prefer a site that allows framing. Of the sites checked when this was written, kubernetes.io, helm.sh, docs.cilium.io, gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io, prometheus.io and etcd.io allowed framing; istio.io (SAMEORIGIN) and docs.docker.com (DENY) did not.
  • docs with file: Markdown shipped with the lab, rendered and sanitised like the task.

astrona validate fails on an unknown type, a field that does not apply to the type, an unknown cluster or port forward, a tcp port forward, a URL that is not https://, a missing, oversized or solution file, a duplicate name and more than 8 tabs.

docs.title: ResourceItem
docs.text:
Shared shape for every script/manifest reference (bootstrap.init, bootstrap.manifests, testing.*, teardown.init, validation.script, validation.scripts).

Field Type Description name string Label printed as the step runs description string Optional, printed alongside name type string "file" | "folder" | "url" (manifests support all three; scripts too). A script folder runs only its regular *.sh files, in filename order — number them (01-x.sh, 02-y.sh) to control ordering; hidden files (.DS_Store, .setup.sh.swp), other extensions (README.md, setup.sh~), subfolders and symlinks are skipped. A manifest folder is handed to kubectl apply -f as is source string Path or URL, depending on type. A file/folder path must be relative to the lab's base directory and stay inside it, also once symlinks are resolved: absolute paths, .. that leaves the lab, and links pointing outside it are refused, by astrona validate as well as at run time. A url source must be https:// (redirects to http:// are refused); scripts and manifests alike are downloaded to a size-capped temp file (50 MiB) and run/applied from there hint string Validation scripts only: shown when the script fails points int Validation scripts only: weight in the score (default 1) timeout duration Scripts only (refused on manifests): how long the entry may run, e.g. 90s, 10m, 1h; between 1s and 2h. A folder source's scripts share one limit. Default 30m for bootstrap/testing/teardown scripts, 5m for validation scripts. See Time limits

docs.title: Time limits
docs.text:
Every script and check has a time limit, so a command that never returns (a kubectl waiting on a cluster that is gone, an ssh that hangs, a sleep infinity) can't hang astrona run, submit, test or destroy. When the limit passes, astrona kills the script or check together with every process it started (its whole process group: no kubectl or ssh is left running), and reports it as timed out after <limit>:

  • a bootstrap/testing script that times out fails the step, like a script that exits non-zero;
  • a teardown script that times out is warned about, like any failed teardown script, and the lab is still destroyed;
  • a validation script or check that times out is a failed check in the report (it earns no points), not a grading error.

On a qemu lab, a script runs over SSH: on timeout the local ssh is killed, which closes the session, and the shell in the VM gets SIGHUP with it.

Item Default Allowed bootstrap.init, testing.init, teardown.init script 30m 1s–2h validation.script / validation.scripts 5m 1s–2h validation.checks entry 1m (http: 10s; podReady: waits 60s) 1s–30m 
bootstrap:
  init:
    - {name: install operator, type: file, source: bootstrap/operator.sh, timeout: 45m}
validation:
  checks:
    - {name: web is ready, type: podReady, resource: pods -l app=web -n shop, timeout: 3m}
  script: {name: content is right, type: file, source: validate.sh, timeout: 30s}

astrona validate rejects a timeout that isn't a duration or is out of range.

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
metadata:
  name: "k8s-basics-01"
  docs:
    prerequisites: "docs/prerequisites.md"
    question: "docs/exam-question.md"
    caseStudy: "docs/case-study.md"
    solution: "docs/step-by-step-guide.md"

bootstrap:
  init:
    - name: "echo"
      type: "file"
      source: "hello.sh"
  manifests: []

testing:
  manifests:
    - name: "solution"
      type: "folder"
      source: "solution"

validation:
  checks:
    - name: "lab-ns namespace exists"
      type: "resourceExists"
      resource: "namespace/lab-ns"
  script:
    type: "file"
    source: "validate.sh"
  scripts:
    - name: "check-network"
      type: "file"
      source: "validate-network.sh"

teardown:
  init:
    - name: "dump-logs"
      type: "file"
      source: "teardown/dump-logs.sh"
  keepCluster: false

For the CLI's own flags and commands, see the CLI Reference.

docs.title: Workspace API
docs.text:
The browser workspace is a small web page served by astrona itself, on 127.0.0.1 only. This page is the contract between that page and the server (internal/workspace). It describes what the server implements today; routes marked later are reserved and answer 404 not_found until they exist.

The server is started on demand by astrona run <lab> (when you answer yes to "Open this lab in your browser?") and stopped by astrona ui stop or after it has been idle for a while; astrona ui <lab> starts it for a running lab. See the browser workspace guide.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Base URL. http://127.0.0.1:<port>. The server prefers port 47300 and takes a free port when that one is in use; the port is recorded in ~/.astrona/workspace/server.json. localhost:<port> is accepted as well; any other Host header is refused with 421.
  • JSON. Request bodies must be Content-Type: application/json, at most 4 KiB, and may not contain unknown fields. Responses are JSON with Cache-Control: no-store.
  • Times are RFC 3339 strings in UTC. Every run response carries serverNow, so the page can compute remaining time from deadlineAt and the offset to its own clock instead of trusting the local clock.
  • Errors always have this shape:
{ "error": "human readable message", "code": "not_started" }
Status code When 400 bad_request Malformed body, wrong content type, unknown field, invalid size. 400 unknown_tab tab is not one of the run's terminal tabs. 400 invalid_idempotency_key POST /submit without an Idempotency-Key of 8 to 128 letters, digits, - or _. 401 unauthorized Missing or invalid token, launch code or ticket. 403 forbidden Not a loopback peer, foreign Origin, cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site. 404 not_found Unknown route, lab, question or terminal. 405 method_not_allowed Method not allowed (OPTIONS included: there is no CORS). 409 run_changed runId in the request is not the lab's current run. Reload the run. 409 not_started Question text or terminals requested before Start. 409 run_stopped The lab is no longer running (stopped, destroyed or restarted). 409 terminal_starting Another request is already starting this tab's terminal. Try again in a few seconds. 409 submit_in_progress The lab is already being submitted (with another Idempotency-Key), or removal was asked for while it is. 409 no_grading POST /submit on a playground: it has no checks. End it with POST /destroy. 409 lab_busy Another astrona command holds the lab's lock. Nothing was graded or sent. 409 not_trusted The lab's scripts were never approved on this machine. Approve it with astrona run in a terminal. 409 environment_kept POST /destroy on a lab from your own files with teardown.keepCluster. Nothing was removed. 404 no_submission GET /submission for a run that was never submitted. 421 unexpected_host Host is not 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port>. 429 too_many_terminals The lab already has 12 open terminals. 500 internal Anything else. The message says what failed. 501 unsupported Terminals on a platform without a PTY (native Windows). 502 terminal_failed The terminal container could not be started. Nothing else was started instead. 500, 502 grading_failed The checks could not run (config not loadable, container engine down). Nothing was recorded or sent; the lab keeps running. 502 destroy_failed Removing the environment failed. The message says what is left. 503 unavailable The server is stopping; no new terminal is started.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
1. The CLI prints and opens a launch URL:
http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#code=<code>&lab=<lab>

The fragment is never sent to the server. code is single-use and valid for two minutes; lab names the run the page should show (absent: show the list from GET /api/v1/runs).

  1. The page exchanges the code and removes the fragment from the address bar:

POST /api/v1/auth/exchange {"code": "<code>"} → 200 {"token": "<token>"}

A used, expired or forged code gives 401 unauthorized.

  1. Every other /api/v1 request sends Authorization: Bearer <token>. There are no cookies. Keep the token in sessionStorage (origin-scoped, port included). A server restart invalidates every token; the page then asks the user to run astrona ui <lab> for a new link.

  2. WebSockets cannot send headers. Fetch a ticket first:

POST /api/v1/auth/ticket (no body) → 200 {"ticket": "<ticket>", "expiresAt": "<time>"}

A ticket is single-use and valid for 30 seconds.

  1. Entering a run from setup or the lab list loads a fresh document so its framing policy includes that run's page tabs:

POST /api/v1/auth/code (bearer token, no body) → 200 {"code": "<code>"}

This code has the same two-minute lifetime and single-use rules as a CLI launch code. The page reloads with it in the fragment and exchanges it as above. This also works when browser storage is disabled and the current bearer token exists only in memory; bearer tokens never go in URLs.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
All paths are under /api/v1 unless they start with /ws/.

Method and path Purpose POST /auth/exchange Launch code → session token. POST /auth/code Authenticated page → single-use launch code for document navigation. POST /auth/ticket Single-use WebSocket ticket. GET /server Version, profile, features. GET /launches/{id} A browser-first astrona run before its lab exists: terms, setup progress, outcome. POST /launches/{id}/terms Accept or decline the CLI terms for that run. GET /labs Every lab on this computer, opened in the browser or not. GET /runs Labs the workspace was opened for. GET /runs/{lab} One run: identity, mode, status, clock, questions, targets, tabs. GET /runs/{lab}/questions/{id} One question rendered to HTML. After Start only. POST /runs/{lab}/start The Start button. Idempotent. GET /runs/{lab}/terminals Open terminals. GET /runs/{lab}/tabs/{name}/doc A docs tab's Markdown, rendered to HTML. After Start only. POST /runs/{lab}/terminals Open the shell of a terminal tab. After Start only. POST /runs/{lab}/submit Grade the run, record and send the result. Needs an Idempotency-Key header. GET /runs/{lab}/submission The run's latest submission, or that one is being graded. POST /runs/{lab}/destroy Remove the environment without grading: ends a playground, or removes a lab as astrona destroy does. GET /ws/v1/terminals/{id}?ticket=… Attach to a terminal (WebSocket). later PUT /runs/{lab}/progress, GET /runs/{lab}/events Not implemented yet.

GET routes never change saved state, so polling them is safe.

docs.title: GET /server
docs.text:
{
  "version": "0.5.0",
  "profile": ".astrona",
  "startedAt": "2026-11-09T21:00:00Z",
  "serverNow": "2026-11-09T21:05:12Z",
  "features": ["runs", "terminals", "tabs", "submit"],
  "assets": "built"
}

assets is "placeholder" when the binary was built without the frontend.

docs.title: GET /launches/{id}
docs.text:
A launch is one interactive astrona run that opened the browser before its lab exists. The page finds it from &launch=<id> in the link (it rewrites the address to #/launches/<id>) and polls this route. astrona run writes the launch; the server only reads it, and notes when the page last asked so the command knows whether the tab is still open.

{
  "schema": 1,
  "id": "3f9c…",
  "pid": 41234,
  "stage": "preparing",
  "title": "Kubernetes playground",
  "events": [
    {"at": "…", "kind": "section", "label": "Cluster"},
    {"at": "…", "kind": "step", "label": "Create kind cluster"},
    {"at": "…", "kind": "ok", "label": "Create kind cluster", "seconds": 41.2}
  ],
  "status": "waiting for CoreDNS · 12s",
  "logPath": "~/.astrona/logs/…",
  "account": { "state": "signed-in", "username": "ada", "site": "https://astrona.io" },
  "alive": true
}
stage Meaning terms Waiting for the terms. terms holds revision, sha256 and text, exactly as the running CLI ships them. checking Resolving the lab. The terminal may ask a question. preparing Building the lab; events and status show progress. ready lab names the run the page opens next (GET /runs/{lab}), after Begin this session. failed error says why. declined The terms were declined; nothing was started. ended The command stopped without a lab for this page; message says why.

alive is false once the astrona run process has exited; with a stage that is not final, the command was stopped. answered (accepted or declined) appears once the terms were answered. At most 200 events are kept. Launches older than a day are removed.

account appears once astrona run has decided whose account the run is saved to, which is after the lab was resolved and the lab session was (or was not) started. The page shows it as a card while the lab is set up. playground: true is set with it when the lab is a playground, which has time but no attempts, so the card does not mention a result.

account.state Meaning signed-in A catalog lab with a lab session: the time and the submitted result, pass or fail, are saved to the account (a playground: the time). username and site say which account. signed-out A catalog lab started without a lab session (not signed in): nothing from this run is saved to an account. site is the site astrona would sign in to, for a sign-up link. local-only Started with --local-only: nothing is sent. untracked A lab from local files or --git: no account applies. The page shows nothing.

account only ever holds state, username and site, never a token, device ID or key ID. site is the site the CLI resolved itself (ASTRONA_URL, then the saved sign-in, then the profile default), never a value from lab content. The state describes this run: signing in later does not change it.

Errors: 404 launch_gone (removed, or never existed).

docs.title: POST /launches/{id}/terms
docs.text:
Request: {"accept": true, "sha256": "<terms.sha256>"}. Writes the answer for the waiting command, which saves the receipt (method browser) or stops.

Response: 200 {"accepted": true}.

Errors: 404 launch_gone; 409 not_asking (not at terms, or the command exited); 409 terms_changed (the digest does not match); 409 answered.

docs.title: GET /labs
docs.text:
Every astrona lab on this computer: Kind clusters and QEMU VMs with this build's prefix, joined with their saved state. Linked clusters (a lab's second cluster) and test clusters are left out.

{
  "labs": [
    { "lab": "astro-pod-basics", "name": "pod-basics", "title": "Pod basics",
      "runtime": "kind", "state": "running", "uptime": "2h", "mode": "learning",
      "playground": false, "workspace": true, "runId": "…", "runStatus": "ready" }
  ],
  "engine": "…"
}

state is running, stopped, degraded (some VMs stopped) or unknown. vms counts a QEMU lab's VMs. deadlineAt is when a playground is deleted or an exam ends. workspace is true when the page has a current run for the lab (GET /runs/{lab}); title, mode, runId and runStatus come from that run. engine is set, with a message, when the container engine does not answer; Kind labs are then missing from the list.

docs.title: GET /runs
docs.text:
{
  "runs": [
    { "lab": "pod-basics", "title": "Pod basics", "mode": "learning",
      "playground": false, "status": "ready" }
  ]
}

docs.title: GET /runs/{lab}
docs.text:
{
  "lab": "pod-basics",
  "runId": "3f1c…64 hex characters…",
  "title": "Pod basics",
  "mode": "exam",
  "playground": false,
  "status": "running",
  "startedAt": "2026-11-09T21:01:00Z",
  "deadlineAt": "2026-11-09T22:31:00Z",
  "timeLimitSeconds": 5400,
  "serverNow": "2026-11-09T21:05:12Z",
  "rules": { "strict": true, "hintsHidden": true },
  "intro": {
    "prerequisitesHtml": "<p>Know what a Pod is.</p>\n",
    "estimatedDuration": "45m"
  },
  "questions": [
    { "id": "q1", "title": "Pod basics", "points": null }
  ],
  "targets": [
    { "name": "pod-basics", "label": "main", "kind": "kind", "views": ["terminal"] }
  ],
  "tabs": [
    { "name": "main", "title": "Terminal", "kind": "terminal", "focus": true, "target": "pod-basics" },
    { "name": "shop", "title": "Shop", "kind": "browser", "focus": false, "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/" },
    { "name": "k8s", "title": "Kubernetes docs", "kind": "docs", "focus": false,
      "url": "https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/" },
    { "name": "notes", "title": "Notes", "kind": "docs", "focus": false, "document": true }
  ],
  "canSubmit": true,
  "submit": {
    "tracking": "account",
    "grading": false,
    "submitted": false,
    "blocked": ""
  },
  "account": { "state": "signed-in", "username": "ada", "site": "https://astrona.io" },
  "runAgain": "astrona run astrona.io/ATS014/section-010/module-01/lab-02"
}
Field Meaning runId Opaque. Send it back on every mutating request. It changes when the lab is restarted, reset to a new session or run from another config. mode exam (the lab has exam.timeLimit) or learning. playground A playground has no intro and no Start: open the workspace directly. status ready (environment up, Start not clicked), running, expired (exam time is over), stopped (the lab is gone or was restarted; this runId is dead). provisioning and failed are reserved for later milestones. startedAt When Start was clicked; null before. deadlineAt null when there is no clock: learning labs, exams before Start, untimed playgrounds. A playground started from the catalog has its session deadline. timeLimitSeconds The exam's time limit, shown on the intro; null for learning labs. rules strict: a submission after the deadline cannot pass. hintsHidden: hints are never shown. intro For the intro page. prerequisitesHtml is "" when the lab has none; estimatedDuration is "" when its task does not say. questions Summaries only, never the text. Today every lab has exactly one question, q1, built from metadata.docs.question. points is null until per-question points exist. targets Where terminals run. kind is kind (a Kind cluster) or vm (one VM of a QEMU lab; name is the VM's handle, the lab name for a single-VM lab or <lab>-<vm>). label is the display name (main, a linked cluster's name, or the VM's name in a multi-VM lab). views lists what the target offers: ["terminal"] today; a desktop will add "desktop". tabs The right panel, as the lab declares it (lab config tabs). The first is always the focus tab: name main, a terminal on the lab's own cluster. The page shows exactly these and cannot add or close one. kind is terminal (target says where its shell runs), browser (url is a loopback port forward of the lab), or docs: either url (an https documentation page, shown in a frame) or document: true (Markdown shipped with the lab, fetched from GET /tabs/{name}/doc). A lab that declares no tabs gets only the focus tab. A QEMU lab cannot declare tabs: a single-VM lab gets the focus tab on its VM, a multi-VM lab gets the focus tab on its first VM (titled with the VM's name) and a terminal tab vm-<name> for each further VM. canSubmit true when POST /submit would grade now: a lab or exam that was started and is still running (an expired exam can still be submitted). Never for a playground. submit.tracking Where a result goes. account: the run has an Astrona lab session; the result is sent when astrona is signed in to that site. local-only: never sent. none: no lab session; the result stays on this machine. submit.grading A submission of this run is being graded now. submit.checks Only while grading, once the checks start: each check and validation script in grading order, as {"name", "state", "startedAt", "seconds"}. state is waiting, running, passed or failed; startedAt is set once it runs, seconds (its duration) once it is done. Never its command or output. Poll GET /runs/{lab} for it while POST /submit waits. submit.submitted This run has a saved result (GET /submission). submit.blocked Why Submit is not possible now, for the page to show next to the disabled button; "" when it is. account Whose account this run is saved to, shown as one line on the intro page; the same object as on GET /launches/{id}. astrona run saves it with the run (runs/<lab>/run.json). A run without one, such as a lab started before this field or reopened with astrona ui, gets signed-in (site only) or local-only from its saved lab session, and no account otherwise. runAgain The command that starts this lab again, as astrona run was given it: the catalog ID, the --git source, or the config path (-c). Never the cluster name, which astrona run does not accept. "" when the source is not known.

Responses never contain the solution document, validation scripts, check commands, expected values, admin credentials or kubeconfigs.

docs.title: GET /runs/{lab}/questions/{id}
docs.text:
{
  "id": "q1",
  "title": "Pod basics",
  "html": "<h1>Pod basics</h1>\n<p>Create a Pod named <code>web</code> …</p>\n",
  "points": null,
  "target": "pod-basics",
  "hints": []
}

html is rendered on the server from the task's Markdown (GitHub-flavoured tables, strikethrough, autolinks and task lists). Raw HTML in the Markdown is dropped, and links with javascript:, vbscript:, file: or data: URLs are removed (except data:image/…, which the CSP's img-src 'self' does not load). Insert it as HTML; the page's CSP blocks inline script anyway. target is the target the question is about. hints is always empty for now.

Before Start an exam or learning lab answers 409 not_started (a playground never does). A question id other than q1 gives 404 not_found.

docs.title: GET /runs/{lab}/tabs/{name}/doc
docs.text:
{ "name": "notes", "title": "Notes", "html": "<h1>Notes</h1>\n<p>…</p>\n" }

Rendered and sanitised like the question. Only for a docs tab with document: true; any other name is 404 not_found. Errors: 409 not_started, 409 run_stopped.

docs.title: POST /runs/{lab}/start
docs.text:
Request: {"runId": "<runId>"}

Response: 200 with the run, exactly as GET /runs/{lab}, now with status: "running" (or "expired"), startedAt and, for an exam, deadlineAt.

Starting is idempotent: a second call, from the same tab or another, returns the run with the deadline the first call set. A runId that is not the current run gives 409 run_changed; a stopped lab gives 409 run_stopped. For a playground Start is accepted and changes nothing.

Only now does the exam clock start (astrona status and astrona submit see it). A run that declined the browser keeps the old behaviour: the clock starts when the lab is ready.

For a run linked to an Astrona lab session, the first Start also tells the site, after start.json is written: POST {site}/api/cli/lab-sessions/{id}/start with {"at": "<startedAt>"}, through the outbox like the other clock signals. It runs in the background and never changes this answer; offline it waits in the outbox, and a failure is a warning in the server log. The site keeps the first start. astrona ui <lab> for an exam whose clock already started at readiness sends the same signal with that time. A local-only or untracked run sends nothing.

docs.title: POST /runs/{lab}/submit
docs.text:
Request: {"runId": "<runId>"} with an Idempotency-Key: <key> header (8 to 128 letters, digits, - or _; the page makes 32 random hex characters per confirmed submission).

It does what astrona submit does, through the same code (labops.Submit), under the lab's lock:

  1. The lab's checks run against the environment.
  2. The result is saved in this machine's attempt history.
  3. It is sent where the run is tracked (submit.tracking). A local-only run is never sent; a run without a lab session stays on this machine.
  4. Every recorded result ends the attempt, pass or fail: one that was sent or queued, or, for a run without a lab session (local-only or none), one saved here. The environment is then removed: terminals are closed first, then the cluster is deleted. teardown.keepCluster does not keep it. Only a tracked result Astrona refuses, or one that cannot be sent or queued, leaves the environment running (finished is false).

Grading can take minutes; the response waits for it. The work does not depend on the request: if the connection drops, grading goes on and GET /submission reports it. Repeating the request with the same key and runId waits for, or returns, the same outcome and never grades twice. A different key while grading runs gives 409 submit_in_progress. The key is only remembered by this server process.

If the checks cannot run (grading_failed, not_trusted, lab_busy), nothing is recorded or sent and the lab keeps running.

Response: 200 with the submission:

{
  "lab": "pod-basics",
  "runId": "3f1c…",
  "result": {
    "pass": true, "earned": 10, "max": 10, "percent": 100, "passPercent": 66,
    "overTime": false, "elapsedSeconds": 754, "attempt": 2, "time": "2026-11-09T21:40:00Z",
    "checks": [
      { "name": "Pod web is running", "pass": true, "points": 6 },
      { "name": "Pod web uses nginx:1.27", "pass": true, "points": 4 }
    ]
  },
  "recorded": true,
  "sent": true,
  "queued": false,
  "finished": true,
  "environmentRemoved": true,
  "messages": ["Sent to your lab page (attempt 2): https://…", "Lab pod-basics deleted."]
}
Field Meaning result.checks Name, pass/fail and points per check. hint only for a failed check of a lab that shows hints. Never the check's command, output or expected value. result.overTime A strict exam submitted after its deadline: it cannot pass. result.elapsedSeconds Time spent on the run until this submission: an exam's clock, otherwise from Start (or from when the lab became ready when it was not started in the workspace). Left out when unknown. recorded Saved in this machine's attempt history. sent Recorded on the Astrona lab page. queued Not sent yet: kept in the outbox and sent once Astrona can be reached. finished The attempt is over, pass or fail: the result was sent or queued, or saved here for a run without a lab session. The environment is then removed. environmentRemoved The cluster was deleted after the submission. messages What astrona said while sending and cleaning up, as sanitised plain text (at most 40 lines). cleanupError Present when the result stands but removing the environment failed.

The latest submission is kept in runs/<lab>/submission.json until the lab is run again.

Errors: 400 invalid_idempotency_key, 409 run_changed, 409 run_stopped, 409 not_started, 409 no_grading, 409 submit_in_progress, 409 lab_busy, 409 not_trusted, 500/502 grading_failed.

docs.title: GET /runs/{lab}/submission
docs.text:
{ "state": "grading" }
{ "state": "failed", "error": { "code": "grading_failed", "message": "…" } }
{ "state": "done", "submission": { …as above… } }

grading while a submission runs, failed when the last one this server ran could not grade, done with the saved result. 404 no_submission when the run was never submitted. Read-only.

docs.title: POST /runs/{lab}/destroy
docs.text:
Request: {"runId": "<runId>"}. No grading, nothing is submitted.

  • A playground is deleted as when the CLI ends it: terminals are closed, the cluster is deleted, and the playground's clock is stopped on the site with a usage report (unless the run is local only). An expired playground can still be ended.
  • A lab is removed as astrona destroy <lab> does: teardown scripts run when the lab is trusted (skipped with a message otherwise), the cluster is deleted, the exam clock is cleared, and the Astrona lab page is told the lab was removed. A lab from your own files with teardown.keepCluster answers 409 environment_kept and nothing is removed; a catalog or tracked lab is always removed.

Response: 200 {"environmentRemoved": true, "messages": ["…"]}.

Errors: 409 run_changed, 409 submit_in_progress, 409 environment_kept, 502 destroy_failed.

docs.title: GET /runs/{lab}/terminals
docs.text:
{
  "terminals": [
    { "id": "Zk3q…", "tab": "main", "target": "pod-basics", "status": "running",
      "exitCode": null, "createdAt": "2026-11-09T21:01:03Z", "attached": true }
  ]
}

status is running or ended; exitCode is set once it ended (-1 when the process was killed by a signal). Ended terminals stay listed until the tab opens a new shell, which replaces the ended one, so the page can show "Shell ended". The page cannot close a terminal; astrona ui stop ends them all.

docs.title: POST /runs/{lab}/terminals
docs.text:
Request: {"runId": "<runId>", "tab": "main"}. tab names one of the run's terminal tabs and may be omitted for the focus tab. The page cannot name a target or anything else: a shell is only ever opened where the lab declared a terminal tab.

Each tab has at most one shell. Response: 200 with the tab's terminal when it is still running (nothing new is started), or 201 with a new one; a new one replaces the tab's ended shell. While one request starts a tab's shell, another for the same tab gets 409 terminal_starting.

On a kind target this can take a minute the first time on a machine, while the terminal image is built. The terminal is a hardened container on the Kind network that mounts only the lab's own workspace directory; its prompt is astrona-cli > and $HOME is /workspace. If the container cannot start, the answer is 502 terminal_failed and nothing else is started in its place.

On a vm target the terminal is an ssh -tt login into that VM as the lab's student user, with the lab's own key and known-hosts file, no SSH config (-F /dev/null), no agent, no forwarding and no escape character, and a 10-second connect timeout. The shell starts in ~/.astrona/runtime/<lab> in the VM. The lab's resources are installed in the student's home first, as for astrona ssh. If that fails, the answer is 502 terminal_failed. If ssh cannot connect, the terminal ends with ssh's error and exit code 255. There is never a fallback to a shell on the host.

Errors: 409 not_started, 409 run_changed, 409 run_stopped, 409 terminal_starting, 400 unknown_tab, 429 too_many_terminals, 501 unsupported.

docs.title: GET /ws/v1/terminals/{id}?ticket=<ticket>
docs.text:
A WebSocket upgrade. The request must carry the page's own Origin (browsers do). Before the upgrade the server answers with a normal HTTP error: 401 unauthorized (missing, used or expired ticket), 404 not_found (unknown terminal), 400 bad_request (not an upgrade).

Frames:

  • Binary frames are terminal bytes, in both directions. Client to server: keyboard input, at most 64 KiB per frame. Server to client: output.
  • Text frames are JSON control messages, never mixed into the byte stream.

Server to client:

Message Meaning {"type":"attached","terminal":{…terminal object…}} Always the first frame. Then the buffered output (up to 1 MiB) follows as binary frames, then live output. Clear the screen before writing the replay. {"type":"ended","exitCode":0} The shell exited. The connection closes with code 1000. {"type":"takenOver"} The same terminal was opened in another tab or view. Closes with 4001. Do not reconnect automatically. {"type":"overrun"} This view fell more than the buffer behind. Closes with 4002; reconnect to get a fresh replay. {"type":"pong"} Answer to a ping. {"type":"error","message":"…"} A control frame was invalid or a resize failed, or input was dropped because a strict exam's time is up. The connection stays open.

Client to server:

Message Meaning {"type":"resize","cols":120,"rows":32} Set the terminal size. Both 1–1000. Send it right after attached and on every resize. {"type":"ping"} Keep-alive; answered with pong.

Other close codes: 1001 when the server shuts down or the terminal is replaced, 1008 for a control frame that is not valid JSON, 1009 for a frame larger than 64 KiB.

In a strict exam the terminal is read-only once the deadline has passed: the server drops keyboard input (and says so once per attachment), while output still flows. Submit still works.

Opening the same terminal again takes it over: only the newest view can type. Closing the WebSocket (tab closed, page reloaded) does not end the shell; reattaching replays its recent output, so the shell and its history survive a reload.

docs.title: Framing
docs.text: The page is served with the strict policy above plus a frame-src that names exactly the origins of the current runs' browser tabs and docs URL tabs, computed when the page is loaded. It never names the server's own origin. Entering a run from setup or the lab list automatically reloads the document, so tabs for labs created after the page opened can be framed. Frames are sandboxed (allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups allow-downloads); nothing is proxied through the server. A site that refuses to be framed (X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors) stays blank; the tab's Open in new window shows it in a separate window instead.

docs.title: Lifetime
docs.text:
• The server writes ~/.astrona/workspace/server.json (mode 0600) with its PID, port and secret, and removes it when it exits.
  • It exits after 15 minutes with no requests, no open WebSocket, no open terminal and no running lab it was opened for. astrona ui stop stops it at once and closes every terminal; labs keep running.
  • If the server process ends, its terminals end with it. The lab, its exam clock and the files under /workspace survive.

docs.title: Where state lives
docs.text:
File Written by Contents ~/.astrona/workspace/server.json server PID, port, start time, version, per-start secret. ~/.astrona/workspace/server.log server Its log. ~/.astrona/workspace/launches/<id>/launch.json astrona run A browser-first run before its lab exists: stage, terms notice, setup progress. ~/.astrona/workspace/launches/<id>/answer.json server The page's answer to the terms. ~/.astrona/workspace/runs/<lab>/run.json astrona run What the page shows for that run: title, mode, rules, the account status, the task and prerequisites Markdown, targets, tabs (with the Markdown of docs tabs). Never the solution or the validation block. ~/.astrona/workspace/runs/<lab>/start.json Start When Start was clicked, for which runId. Removed when the lab is deleted (submit, destroy, reset, expiry). astrona submit uses it only while its runId is the lab's current run and it is not earlier than the lab became ready. ~/.astrona/workspace/runs/<lab>/submission.json Submit The latest browser submission for that runId: the result as GET /submission shows it.

The whole runs/<lab>/ folder is removed when the lab is started again, from a terminal or the browser, so a new run never inherits an earlier run's record, Start or result. | ~/.astrona/exams/<lab>.json | Start (exam labs) | The exam clock, as before. |

Other profiles use their own home (~/.astrona-dev/…).

docs.text: Let the Astrona website start labs on this computer

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Keep this computer connected to the Astrona site, so "Start on my machine" on a lab page builds the lab here. Runs until Ctrl+C, reconnecting by itself after a drop.

The website can only ask for run, status, submit, reset, destroy, stop, start and renew (a running playground's full time limit again), each for a catalog lab by name; astrona checks both before anything runs. Nothing else travels over the connection: no shell commands, files or URLs.

--install starts it with your login session from now on (a LaunchAgent on macOS, a systemd user service on Linux); --uninstall removes that again. Its log is ~/.astrona/logs/connect.log.

--confirm asks at this terminal before each request from the website runs (status needs no answer). A request you decline, or leave unanswered for two minutes, is refused, and the website says so.

Signing this computer out on the website ends the connection and removes the sign-in here.

astrona connect [flags]

docs.title: astrona destroy
docs.text: Remove a lab and everything in it (and any leftover astrona test copy)

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Tear down a lab environment (both the normal run and any leftover 'astrona test' run).

With no lab-name, resolves the lab config the same way run/submit do (-c/--file/--git/--git-ref) and falls back to auto-discovering running labs only when no source was selected. An unreadable explicit config, catalog lab or saved selection fails without destroying another lab.

With a lab-name (as shown by astrona list, with or without the 'astro-' prefix — e.g. 'astro-my-lab' or just 'my-lab'), destroys that lab directly — no config needed, so -c/--file/--git/--git-ref are ignored and any teardown scripts are skipped.

With a catalog name (astrona.io/ATS016/section-020/module-01/lab-01, or without astrona.io/ as astrona labs lists it), destroys that lab through its config, teardown scripts included.

With a glob pattern (contains *, ?, or [), matches against all currently-running lab names (same list astrona list shows, with or without the 'astro-' prefix) and destroys every match — e.g. astrona destroy 'qemu-jumphost-*' (quote it so your shell doesn't expand the glob itself). No config needed, same trade-offs as a single name.

A lab's linked clusters (runtime.kind.clusters) are destroyed with it.

If astrona run pointed kubectl at the lab, the kubectl context you had before comes back — only when the lab's context is still current (if you've switched elsewhere, that's left as it is). What astrona remembered about the lab (its config, its lab session) is forgotten.

A remote lab (--git, URL, catalog) that has teardown scripts asks for approval first, like run — --trust approves it up front. If it isn't approved (declined, or no terminal and no --trust), its teardown scripts are skipped and the lab is still destroyed.

The lab's copy of its resources (~/.astrona/resources/) is removed too; --keep-resources keeps it.

Port forwards of the lab are always stopped, even when its cluster or VM is already gone.

Ctrl+C (or SIGTERM) stops only the step that is running: astrona carries on with the remaining steps, so less is left behind. A second Ctrl+C quits at once.

astrona destroy [lab-name|pattern] [flags]

docs.title: astrona exam
docs.text: Take a full lab exam: several tasks on prepared clusters, against the clock

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Take a full lab exam, such as the CKS practice exam, on this computer.

astrona exam start checks that the exam's clusters fit your container engine, draws the tasks, builds the clusters in parallel and applies every task's setup. The clock does not run while it prepares: it starts when you press Begin exam on the exam page. Each task names the kubectl context to use (exam-1, exam-2, ...); switching to it is up to you, as in the real exam.

Work on the tasks in any order. Take up to the exam's number of breaks (astrona exam break); a break pauses every exam cluster. astrona exam submit, or the deadline, grades every task on its cluster, sends the results and deletes the clusters. Results show on the exam page.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
astrona exam start cks
  astrona exam status
  astrona exam task 3
  astrona exam next
  astrona exam break
  astrona exam resume
  astrona exam submit

docs.title: astrona exam start
docs.text: Prepare a full lab exam's clusters and open the exam page

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Prepare a full lab exam on this computer.

The exam's clusters must fit within 75% of your container engine's memory, counting other kind clusters that are running; if they don't, nothing is started and astrona says how much memory the exam needs. Otherwise the tasks are drawn, the clusters are built (up to --parallel at once) and each task's setup is applied to its cluster. If anything fails, every exam cluster is deleted and the attempt is not counted.

The clock starts when you press Begin exam on the exam page, not before. A watchdog keeps running in the background: it pauses and unpauses the clusters for breaks, and at the deadline grades every task and deletes the clusters.

astrona exam start <exam> [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
astrona exam start cks
  astrona exam start cks --parallel 2

docs.title: astrona labs
docs.text: Browse the lab catalog: trainings and their labs, runnable by name

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
List the trainings astrona knows — the astrona-io repositories with the astrona-training topic, plus sources you add (astrona labs add) — or one training's labs. Every lab has a catalog name you can run, use or test directly:

astrona labs trainings astrona labs ATS014 its labs astrona labs --search routing search lab titles astrona run astrona.io/ATS014/section-010/module-01/lab-02 astrona run astrona.io/ATS014/section-010/module-01/playground

The name may start with the organization — astrona.io/ (as astrona.io shows it) or the GitHub owner astrona-io/ — or leave it out (ATS014/…); another owner is refused. A module's playground is found by its folder.

A lab from the catalog is a remote lab: it's fetched with git and asks for your trust before it runs, like any --git lab. An official (astrona-io) lab runs without asking only when its commit is the one astrona.io publishes for the training and the checkout is unchanged; anything else asks as usual. The catalog is cached for an hour (--refresh reads it again).

astrona labs [training] [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
astrona labs
  astrona labs ATS014
  astrona labs --search "fault injection"
  astrona use astrona.io/ATS014/section-010/module-01/lab-02

docs.title: astrona login
docs.text: Sign in to your Astrona account (catalog labs need it)

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Sign this computer in to your Astrona account. Catalog labs (astrona run astrona.io/ATS014/…) are tied to your account: astrona run starts a lab session for you and opens the lab page, which tracks your time. Labs from your own files or repositories (-c / --git) don't need it.

Sign-in happens on the configured Astrona website: astrona opens its sign-in page in your browser. If you're already signed in there, check that the code matches the one in the terminal and click Authorize; otherwise sign in on that site first and you're brought back to that page. The terminal waits and finishes by itself. No password is ever typed into the terminal. On a machine without a browser, open the printed link on any device. --headless prints the link without opening a browser.

The sign-in is saved in ~/.astrona/credentials.json (readable only by you) and renewed automatically. Each sign-in also makes a device key for this computer, kept in ~/.astrona/device-key.json (readable only by you): the site gets only its public half and checks that every call comes from this computer. astrona whoami shows who is signed in, astrona logout signs out.

The default site is https://astrona.io unless --site (or ASTRONA_URL) names another, for example http://localhost:3000 for local development. The site is remembered with the sign-in, so whoami, logout and catalog labs use it without repeating it; ASTRONA_URL still overrides it per command. Plain http:// is only accepted for localhost.

astrona login [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
astrona login
  astrona login --site http://localhost:3000     # local development; remembered
  ASTRONA_URL=https://staging.astrona.io astrona whoami

docs.title: astrona net
docs.text: Change network conditions of a running lab's cluster (latency, loss, partition)

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Change the network conditions of one cluster of a running kind lab — a linked cluster (--cluster , runtime.kind.clusters) or, without --cluster, the lab's own — to simulate a slow or flaky remote site, or cut it off entirely:

--latency/--jitter/--loss/--rate set conditions (tc netem on every node of the cluster) --partition drop everything it sends (100% loss) — it's unreachable --heal back to the lab config's wan conditions (or none) --show print what each node currently has

Latency is added once per round trip (it delays what the cluster sends). Changes last until --heal, astrona start (which re-applies the config) or the lab is destroyed. While a cluster is partitioned, astrona can't reach its API either.

astrona net [lab-name] [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
astrona net my-lab --cluster idp --latency 300ms --jitter 50ms --loss 5%
  astrona net my-lab --cluster idp --partition
  astrona net my-lab --cluster idp --heal

docs.text:

docs.title: astrona reset
docs.text: Start a lab over: destroy it and recreate it from its config

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Start a lab over from scratch: run its teardown scripts, destroy it, then do everything astrona run does — the lab ends up exactly as a fresh astrona run leaves it. If the lab isn't running, it's simply created.

The config is validated before anything is destroyed, so a broken config never leaves you without a lab. teardown.keepCluster is ignored — reset always recreates.

Asks for confirmation (everything done in the lab is lost); --yes skips it and is required with --headless or when not running in a terminal. --headless also skips the login reminder and new account sessions.

--cluster rebuilds only that linked cluster (runtime.kind.clusters) of a running lab: its teardown scripts, destroy, then create and bootstrap it again (with the addresses of the clusters it dependsOn). The lab and its other clusters are left alone; port forwards into the rebuilt cluster are restarted.

A full reset of a catalog lab asks for confirmation when signed out, like astrona run (--without-login confirms without prompting). When signed in, it starts a fresh session and reports when the rebuilt lab is ready for its course page. --soft and --cluster keep the current session and need no sign-in.

Like astrona run, a full reset points kubectl at the lab (the context to go back to is still the one from before the lab first ran); --keep-context leaves it alone.

--soft keeps the clusters: it deletes every namespace created after the platform (kube-system, addons, …) was set up, clears what isn't astrona's from the default namespace, and runs the bootstrap again — seconds instead of minutes. Cluster-wide objects (CRDs, ClusterRoles, …) aren't reverted; use a full reset for those. With --cluster, only that linked cluster.

Ctrl+C (or SIGTERM) during a full reset or a --cluster rebuild stops at the current step and removes what the rebuild created, like astrona run; a second Ctrl+C quits at once.

astrona reset [lab] [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
astrona reset -c ./labs/my-lab
  astrona reset -c ./labs/my-lab --yes
  astrona reset -c ./labs/my-lab --cluster idp
  astrona reset -c ./labs/my-lab --soft

docs.text:
--cluster string   Rebuild only this linked cluster (its runtime.kind.clusters name)
